summary: Indonesia offers a Visa on Arrival — or its online e-VOA version — of IDR 500,000 for 30 days, extendable once, to citizens of 97 countries and territories, admits ASEAN neighbors and a few other countries (including Brazil and Turkey) visa-free, and requires every arrival to submit a free customs declaration online before landing.

declarations.name: All Indonesia arrival card
declarations.text: The immigration e-Visa portal states that all travellers are required to submit an arrival card within 3 days before arriving in Indonesia. It is filed on the immigration authority's All Indonesia site (allindonesia.imigrasi.go.id).

source.name: Directorate General of Immigration — official e-Visa portal home page (arrival card notice)

declarations.name: Electronic Customs Declaration (e-CD)
declarations.text: All arriving passengers must submit a customs declaration online and show the QR code on landing. It is free. Arrivals by air or sea file it within the All Indonesia arrival card (allindonesia.imigrasi.go.id); arrivals by land use the customs e-CD site (ecd.beacukai.go.id). Use only these official sites.

source.name: Directorate General of Customs and Excise — Electronic Customs Declaration

declarations.name: Bali Tourist Levy (Love Bali)

fee.notes: One-off levy per foreign visitor to Bali; pay online in advance or on arrival.

declarations.submitWindow: Before or on arrival in Bali
declarations.text: Applies only to foreign tourists visiting Bali province, not to the rest of Indonesia. Pay once per trip, cashless: online via the official Love Bali site before you travel (which the provincial government strongly encourages), at the payment counters at Bali's airport and ports, or through hotels, travel agents and attractions registered with Love Bali. The levy voucher with a QR code is sent to the email you enter.

source.name: Love Bali (Bali Provincial Government) — FAQ on the Foreign Tourist Levy
source.instrument: Bali Provincial Regulation No. 2 of 2025 amending Regulation No. 6 of 2023 on the Foreign Tourist Levy; Bali Governor Regulation No. 25 of 2025

currencyLimits.text: Cash or bearer instruments of IDR 100,000,000 or more (or the equivalent in foreign currency) must be declared on arrival and departure.

source.name: Directorate General of Customs and Excise — arriving in Indonesia

notes: Indonesian customs allows each passenger personal goods worth up to USD 500 duty-free; each adult may also bring at most 200 cigarettes, 25 cigars or 100 g of tobacco, and 1 liter of alcoholic drink. Excess excise goods are destroyed by officers.

The UK Foreign Office warns that possessing, using, making or trafficking illegal drugs can bring long prison sentences or the death penalty, and that all cannabis products, including CBD, are illegal. The Government of Canada notes that medicines containing morphine or codeine are controlled substances in Indonesia and cannot be brought in without prior permission from the Ministry of Health.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says credit cards are not widely accepted outside large urban centres and tourist areas, and advises carrying cash when visiting remote areas. The UK Foreign Office warns that credit card fraud is common and advises using only licensed money changers, identified by a Bank Indonesia logo and a QR code.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office warns of bag-snatching and pickpocketing in busy tourist areas, drink spiking, methanol poisoning from counterfeit spirits, and volcanic eruptions, and advises respecting exclusion zones.

source.name: UK FCDO — Indonesia travel advice: safety and security

bestTimeToVisit.text: The UK Foreign Office says the rainy season usually runs from October to March, but in Eastern Indonesia the wet season usually runs from April to August; wildfires and smoke haze are worst in the dry season, usually April to September. The Government of Canada notes that heavy rain is common throughout the year.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office advises using only the Indonesian immigration website (evisa.imigrasi.go.id) to get or extend a visa, says the All Indonesia arrival card is free, and warns against alternative websites or email links that ask for payment, and against fake visa agents.
The UK Foreign Office warns that Indonesia has a zero-tolerance policy on illegal drugs: possession, use, making or trafficking can bring long prison sentences or the death penalty.
The UK Foreign Office says overstaying costs IDR 1,000,000 a day and can lead to prosecution, detention and deportation, and advises extending a 30-day visa within the first 30 days.
Visiting Bali? The provincial government strongly encourages paying the IDR 150,000 tourist levy online before departure at lovebali.baliprov.go.id; the levy voucher with a QR code is sent by email.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Indonesia?
faq.answer: US passport holders can get a Visa on Arrival for IDR 500,000, valid for a 30-day stay and extendable once for another 30 days. It can also be applied for online in advance as an e-VOA at evisa.imigrasi.go.id.

faq.question: Can I extend the Indonesian Visa on Arrival?
faq.answer: Yes, once, for up to 60 days in total. E-VOA holders can extend online at evisa.imigrasi.go.id; holders of a VOA bought on arrival apply at the nearest immigration office.

faq.question: What is the e-CD and who must complete it?
faq.answer: Every passenger arriving in Indonesia must submit a customs declaration. It is free and can be completed from 3 days before arrival; show the QR code to customs officers when you land. Arrivals by air or sea complete it as part of the All Indonesia arrival card (allindonesia.imigrasi.go.id); arrivals by land use the e-CD at ecd.beacukai.go.id.

faq.question: What is the Bali tourist levy?
faq.answer: Foreign tourists visiting Bali pay a one-off levy of IDR 150,000 via the official Love Bali portal (lovebali.baliprov.go.id), or at the payment counters at Bali's airport and ports.

faq.question: Who can enter Indonesia without any visa?
faq.answer: Citizens of ASEAN member states — including the Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia — and of Brazil, Turkey, Colombia, Peru, Suriname, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Hong Kong and Macau enter visa-free for up to 30 days. This visa-free entry cannot be extended or converted to another permit.
